findings.quote:
metrics = {
            "coverage": self.coverage(),
            "validity": self.validity(),
            "actionability": self.actionability(),
            "sparsity": self.sparsity(eps=self.sparsity_eps),
            # "target_distance": self.target_distance(),
            # "proximity_categorical_hamming": self.feature_distance(
            #     categorical_metric="hamming"
            # ),
            # "proximity_categorical_jaccard": self.feature_distance(
            #     categorical_metric="jaccard"
            # ),
            "proximity_continuous_manhattan": self.feature_distance(
                continuous_metric="cityblock"
            ),
findings.claim: calc_all_metrics (the only metric aggregator, called from evaluate_counterfactuals) computes coverage/validity/actionability/sparsity/proximity/LOF/log-density but no hypervolume; a repo-wide grep for hypervol|pareto|dominat returns no matches.
findings.concern: Diversity via Hypervolume is a headline metric reported in Tables 1, 3, 6 and 8 and underpins the paper's central 'superior diversity' claim, yet nothing in the repository computes it, so those numbers cannot be reproduced or checked.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add or point to the script that computes the Hypervolume (diversity) column for every table; state the reference point and objective axes used.
findings.reason: Quote at lines 359-373 matches exactly and a repo-wide grep for hypervol, pareto, and dominat returns zero hits confirming no hypervolume implementation exists.

findings.title: generative_models package imports a nonexistent nice.py, crashing on import
findings.claim: The package __init__ imports NICE from counterfactuals.generative_models.nice, but no nice.py exists in the repo (find -name nice.py returns nothing; the directory holds only base.py, cnf/, kde.py, maf.py, real_nvp.py).
findings.concern: Importing the package (which happens for any submodule, including the driver's `from counterfactuals.generative_models.maf import MaskedAutoregressiveFlow`) raises ModuleNotFoundError, so the committed code cannot run at all; it also means the NICE flow compared in Table 5 (Appendix D) has no implementation.
findings.resolution: Authors: restore counterfactuals/generative_models/nice.py (the NICE flow) or remove the dead import; confirm which commit reproduces Table 5.
findings.reason: Line 5 of __init__.py exactly matches the quote and the generative_models directory contains only base.py, cnf/, kde.py, maf.py, real_nvp.py — nice.py is absent.

findings.title: MLP predict_proba uses ReLU-normalised logits, not its own softmax head
findings.claim: The classifier is trained with CrossEntropyLoss (softmax) and defines self.final_activation = Softmax, but predict_proba turns raw logits into 'probabilities' with relu(logits)+1e-8 normalised to sum 1, and predict() takes argmax over these.
findings.concern: When all class logits are negative for a sample, ReLU maps them to 0 and the sample is forced to class 0 (argmax of a uniform vector), so predict() disagrees with the true argmax; these predictions define the training labels, the validity metric, and the prob_threshold neighbour filter (generic_counterfactual.py:96), biasing the whole pipeline toward class 0.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm whether predict_proba should apply softmax (self.final_activation); quantify how many labels/validity decisions change between softmax and relu-normalised outputs.
findings.reason: Lines 95-105 exactly match the quote; relu(forward(X_test))+1e-8 normalisation is confirmed in place of softmax.

findings.title: MaskedAutoregressiveFlow class actually builds a RealNVP, not a MAF
findings.quote:
model = _SimpleRealNVP(
            features=features,
            hidden_features=hidden_features,
            context_features=context_features,
            num_layers=num_layers,
            num_blocks_per_layer=num_blocks_per_layer,
            activation=activation,
            use_volume_preserving=False,
            dropout_probability=dropout_probability,
            batch_norm_within_layers=batch_norm_within_layers,
            batch_norm_between_layers=batch_norm_between_layers,
        )

        super().__init__(
            transform=model._transform,
            distribution=StandardNormalWithTemp([features]),
        )
findings.claim: The class named MaskedAutoregressiveFlow — used as the flow for every reported DiCoFlex result (train_generic_counterfactual.py:20,75,182) — constructs nflows.SimpleRealNVP and uses its coupling transform; the imported MaskedAffineAutoregressiveTransform (maf.py:11) is never used.
findings.concern: Section 3.2 states 'we selected MAF as our normalizing flow model' and Appendix D / Table 5 justifies this by MAF's NLL (-43.30) being far better than RealNVP (26.58), yet the model the code trains is RealNVP, so the headline numbers were not produced by MAF and the model-selection ablation contradicts the shipped architecture.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm whether the reported results use MAF or RealNVP; if MAF, provide the code path that instantiates MaskedAffineAutoregressiveTransform.
findings.reason: Lines 130-146 exactly match the quote; _SimpleRealNVP is constructed inside MaskedAutoregressiveFlow confirming the wrong architecture is instantiated.

findings.title: ε-sparsity computed as absolute threshold over all features, not relative per continuous feature
findings.claim: The only sparsity metric (called with eps=0.05 from utils.py:94) counts, over ALL features jointly, entries whose ABSOLUTE difference exceeds 0.05.
findings.concern: Paper Eq. 30 defines ε-sparsity as a RELATIVE change |x−x′|/|x| > ε averaged over CONTINUOUS features only, and Eq. 29 defines a separate categorical sparsity; the implemented metric is neither (absolute, not relative; mixed cat+cont), so Table 1's 'Sparsity cat.' and 'ε-sparsity cont.' columns are not produced by this code.
findings.resolution: Authors: point to the code computing the per-type sparsity (Eq. 29) and the relative ε-sparsity (Eq. 30) reported in Table 1, or reconcile the definitions.
findings.paper_ref: Appendix C, Eq. 29-30; Table 1 sparsity columns
findings.reason: Lines 187-193 match exactly; absolute np.abs difference over all features is confirmed with no per-type or relative computation.

findings.title: Adult loader subsamples to 2000 rows; paper reports 32,000
findings.claim: The Adult loader keeps a random 2000-row sample of each of train and test; the other four loaders use their full CSVs.
findings.concern: Paper Table 4 states Adult uses 32,000 samples, but the committed loader uses 2000, so the many Adult-based results (Tables 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7) cannot be reproduced at the stated sample size and are additionally sensitive to the unseeded sample() draw.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm the sample size used for the reported Adult results and whether sample() should be removed or seeded.
findings.reason: Line 81 exactly matches raw_data.sample(2000) confirming the hard-coded 2000-row subsample.

findings.title: Bank loader concatenates test into the training set (test ⊂ train)
findings.quote:
X_all = np.concatenate([self.X_train, self.X_test], axis=0)
        y_all = np.concatenate([self.y_train, self.y_test], axis=0)
        self.X_train, self.y_train = X_all, y_all
findings.claim: In BankDataset.__init__, X_train/y_train are replaced by the concatenation of train and test, while X_test is left as the test set, so the training set contains the entire test set; the other four loaders do not do this.
findings.concern: The classifier, the counterfactual flow, and the plausibility model are all trained on data that includes every test point used for evaluation (and the MinMax/OneHot/Quantile transformers are fit on train+test), so the Bank row of Table 1 (and Bank in Table 7 / Fig 3b) is measured under train/test leakage and does not reflect generalisation.
findings.resolution: Authors: remove the train+test concatenation and re-run Bank; report whether the Bank metrics change once the test set is excluded from training and transformer fitting.
findings.reason: Lines 36-38 exactly match; X_train is overwritten with concatenated train+test while X_test remains, confirming full train-test leakage.
